Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 1) Highest risk period for teratogenesis is:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Organogenesis is the highest-risk period for teratogenesis. It occurs around 4–10 weeks from LMP. Drug avoidance is especially important during this period.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 2) Pregnancy usually causes volume of distribution to:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Pregnancy increases volume of distribution. This is due to increased body fluid and physiological changes. Drug concentration may be altered.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 3) Pregnancy usually causes plasma albumin concentration to:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Plasma albumin decreases in pregnancy. This may increase free fraction of some protein-bound drugs. Clinical effect depends on drug and clearance.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 4) Pregnancy usually causes GFR to:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Pregnancy increases GFR. Renal clearance of some drugs may increase. Dose requirement may change for selected drugs.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 5) Placenta contributes to drug:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Placenta contributes to drug metabolism and clearance. It is not just a passive barrier. Placental transfer is important in fetal drug exposure.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 6) General prescribing principle in pregnancy is:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.option2: Avoid drugs unless benefits outweigh risks
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Drugs should be avoided in pregnancy unless clearly needed. Benefit must outweigh fetal and maternal risk. Safer drugs with established safety records are preferred.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 7) Drug use in pregnancy should generally follow:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.option1: Lowest effective dose for shortest duration
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Pregnancy prescribing should be cautious. Use the lowest effective dose. Use it for the shortest necessary duration.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 8) Labetalol is classified as:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Labetalol blocks alpha and beta receptors. It is commonly used for hypertension in pregnancy. It is listed among safe antihypertensives.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 9) Nifedipine and amlodipine are:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Nifedipine and amlodipine are calcium channel blockers. They are listed as antihypertensive drugs in pregnancy. Nifedipine is commonly used clinically.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 10) Methyldopa acts mainly by:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.option1: Blocking alpha and beta receptors equally
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Methyldopa has central action. It is a traditional antihypertensive used in pregnancy. It has an established safety record.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 11) Which drug group is contraindicated in pregnancy?
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: ACE inhibitors and ARBs should be avoided in pregnancy. They can cause fetal renal failure and fetal loss. Safer alternatives include labetalol, methyldopa and nifedipine.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 12) NSAIDs should be avoided late in pregnancy mainly because of risk of:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: NSAIDs are avoided after 28 weeks. Indomethacin is classically linked with premature ductus closure. Late pregnancy use needs special caution.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 13) Azathioprine in pregnancy and breastfeeding is classified as:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Azathioprine is listed as safe in pregnancy. It is also listed as safe in breastfeeding. It may be used when clinically indicated.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 14) Hydroxychloroquine in pregnancy and breastfeeding is:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Hydroxychloroquine is safe in pregnancy and breastfeeding. It is used in RA and SLE. Stopping it unnecessarily may worsen disease control.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 15) Sulfasalazine in pregnancy and breastfeeding is:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Sulfasalazine is safe in pregnancy and breastfeeding. Folic acid should be co-prescribed. It is used in rheumatologic disease.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 16) Leflunomide in pregnancy and breastfeeding should be:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Leflunomide should be avoided in pregnancy and breastfeeding. It should be stopped 2 years before planning pregnancy unless washout is used. This is a high-yield safety point.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 17) Methotrexate in pregnancy and breastfeeding should be:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Methotrexate is contraindicated in pregnancy. It is also avoided during breastfeeding. It can cause fetal malformations and neural tube defects.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 18) Mycophenolate in pregnancy and breastfeeding should be:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Mycophenolate should be avoided in pregnancy. It should also be avoided during breastfeeding. It should be stopped before planning pregnancy.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 19) Cyclophosphamide in pregnancy and breastfeeding is:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Cyclophosphamide should be avoided in pregnancy. It is also avoided during breastfeeding. It has major fetal and maternal toxicity concerns.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 20) TNF inhibitors in late pregnancy may require avoiding live vaccines in the infant for:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: TNF inhibitors are listed as safe in pregnancy and breastfeeding. But when used late in pregnancy, live vaccines in neonate may be avoided for 6 months. This depends on drug timing and clinical context.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 21) Tetracycline exposure in pregnancy may cause:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.option4: Yellow-brown teeth discoloration and skeletal growth depression
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Tetracycline affects teeth and bone. It may cause yellow-brown teeth discoloration. Skeletal growth depression may also occur.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 22) Chloramphenicol in fetus/neonate is associated with:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Chloramphenicol can cause gray baby syndrome. This occurs due to immature neonatal metabolism. It is a classic fetal/neonatal drug effect.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 23) Aminoglycosides in pregnancy may cause congenital:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Aminoglycosides may damage fetal ear and kidney. Congenital ototoxicity is a key concern. Nephrotoxicity may also occur.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 24) Sulfonamides in fetus/neonate may cause:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Sulfonamides can cause kernicterus. They may displace bilirubin from albumin. They are avoided near term.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 25) Fluoroquinolones in pregnancy may cause:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Fluoroquinolones are associated with cartilage and joint problems. Arthropathy is the key fetal concern. Safer antibiotics are preferred in pregnancy.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 26) Fluconazole exposure may cause:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Fluconazole is linked with Antley-Bixler-like syndrome. It may involve craniofacial, skeletal and cardiac abnormalities. Risk is especially important with high-dose/prolonged exposure.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 27) Phenytoin exposure in pregnancy may cause:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Phenytoin may cause fetal hydantoin syndrome. Features include cleft lip/palate, microcephaly, hypoplastic nails and cardiac defect. It is a classic teratogenic antiepileptic.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 28) Warfarin exposure in pregnancy may cause:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.option1: Depressed nasal bridge with eye/hand defects
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Warfarin crosses the placenta. It can cause fetal warfarin syndrome. Heparin is safer because it does not cross placenta significantly.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 29) Lithium exposure in pregnancy may cause:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Lithium can affect fetal thyroid and heart. Cardiac anomaly is an important concern. Use requires careful risk-benefit assessment.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 30) Antithyroid drugs in pregnancy may cause fetal:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Antithyroid drugs can cross placenta. They may suppress fetal thyroid function. Fetal goitre and hypothyroidism may occur.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 31) Carbamazepine exposure is associated with:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Carbamazepine is associated with neural tube defects. Spina bifida is an important concern. Folic acid supplementation and careful planning are important.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 32) Valproate exposure is associated with:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.option1: Spina bifida, neural tube defect and cardiac abnormality
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Valproate is highly teratogenic. It is strongly associated with neural tube defects. Cardiac abnormalities may also occur.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 33) Thalidomide exposure causes:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Thalidomide classically causes phocomelia. Phocomelia means seal-like limbs. It is one of the most famous teratogenic drug effects.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 34) Trimethoprim exposure is associated with:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Trimethoprim may cause neural tube defects. It interferes with folate metabolism. Folic acid status is important.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 35) Testosterone or androgen exposure may cause:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Androgens may masculinize a female fetus. Virilization is the key fetal effect. Progestins may also cause virilization.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 36) ACE inhibitors in pregnancy may cause:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.option2: Fetal renal failure and fetal loss
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: ACE inhibitors are contraindicated in pregnancy. They may cause fetal renal failure. Organ/skull/lung hypoplasia and fetal loss may occur.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 37) Diazepam exposure near delivery may cause:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Diazepam may cause floppy infant syndrome. Features include hypotonia, hypothermia and respiratory depression. Cleft lip/palate is also listed.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 38) Methotrexate exposure may cause:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.option4: Dysmorphism, neural tube defect, hydrocephalus and cleft palate
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Methotrexate is teratogenic. It may cause dysmorphism and neural tube defects. Hydrocephalus and cleft palate are also listed.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 39) Progestin exposure may cause:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Progestins may virilize a female fetus. Androgens/testosterone can also cause this effect. Hormonal drug exposure must be assessed carefully.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 40) Diethylstilbestrol exposure is associated with:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.option4: Vaginal carcinoma in teenage female offspring
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: DES exposure is linked to clear-cell vaginal carcinoma. It appears later in female offspring. This is a classic delayed teratogenic outcome.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 41) Indomethacin exposure may cause:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Indomethacin is an NSAID. Late pregnancy use can close ductus arteriosus prematurely. NSAIDs are avoided after 28 weeks.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 42) Drugs associated with neural tube defects include:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Neural tube defect-associated drugs include methotrexate and antiepileptics. Valproate, carbamazepine and phenytoin are important. Trimethoprim and retinoids are also listed.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 43) First-line antihypertensive in pregnancy from the high-yield summary is:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Labetalol is listed as first-line antihypertensive. Methyldopa and nifedipine are also safe options. ACE inhibitors and ARBs are avoided.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 44) Safe antihypertensives in pregnancy include:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Labetalol, methyldopa and nifedipine are safe antihypertensive options. They have established pregnancy use. ACE inhibitors and ARBs are contraindicated.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 45) Live vaccines in pregnancy are generally:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Live vaccines are listed among substances crossing the placental barrier. They are generally avoided during pregnancy. The concern is possible fetal infection or harm.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 46) Which statement is correct?
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.option1: Warfarin crosses placenta; heparin does not
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.option2: Both heparin and warfarin are equally teratogenic
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Warfarin crosses placenta and can harm the fetus. Heparin does not significantly cross placenta. So heparin is preferred when anticoagulation is needed in pregnancy.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 47) NSAIDs in antirheumatic pregnancy guidance are:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.option1: Safe before 28 weeks but avoided late pregnancy
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.option4: Safe only during breastfeeding, never pregnancy
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: NSAIDs are listed as safe before 28 weeks. They should be avoided late in pregnancy. The key concern is premature ductus arteriosus closure.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 48) Glucocorticoids in pregnancy and breastfeeding are listed as:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Glucocorticoids are safe in pregnancy and breastfeeding. They are useful as short-term options for disease flares. Dose and duration should still be minimized.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 49) Tacrolimus in pregnancy and breastfeeding is listed as:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Tacrolimus is listed as safe in pregnancy. It is also safe during breastfeeding. Monitoring is still needed because it is an immunosuppressant.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 50) Ciclosporin in pregnancy and breastfeeding is listed as:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.option2: Safe in both, but breastfeeding data limited
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Ciclosporin is listed as safe in pregnancy and breastfeeding. However, breastfeeding data are limited. Clinical decision should consider maternal need and infant monitoring.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 51) Hydroxychloroquine is safe in pregnancy and is commonly useful in:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Hydroxychloroquine is safe in pregnancy and breastfeeding. It is useful in RA and SLE. It helps maintain disease control.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 52) Sulfasalazine in pregnancy should be given with:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Sulfasalazine is safe in pregnancy. Folic acid should be co-prescribed. This reduces folate-related risk.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 53) Which set includes drugs associated with neural tube defects?
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Retinoids are listed among drugs associated with neural tube defects. Valproate and carbamazepine are also important. Trimethoprim is another folate-related risk drug.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 54) Decreased plasma albumin in pregnancy may increase:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Lower albumin means less binding capacity. This may increase free fraction of protein-bound drugs. Clinical significance depends on clearance and therapeutic index.

Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.question: 55) The best general prescribing principle in pregnancy is:
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.option2: Choose the least harmful effective alternative
Drugs effects on pregnancy & Lactations,.exp: Pregnancy prescribing should minimize fetal and maternal harm. Use drugs with established safety records. Choose the least harmful effective option at the lowest effective dose.
